issues.description: Method getLectureName(): In the solution (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java) the getter method is declared to return String (signature: public String getLectureName()) but its implementation returns the field lectureName which is declared as type LectureName. The problem statement UML declares lectureName as a String. This mismatch causes a compilation error and prevents students from using the expected String-based getter described in the exercise.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the lectureName type consistent. Prefer matching the problem statement: change the field and constructor parameter from LectureName to String, and ensure getLectureName() returns that String (adjust return statement). Alternatively, if LectureName is intended, change the getter signature to public LectureName getLectureName() and update the problem statement/tests accordingly. The simplest fix for this exercise is to use String for lectureName throughout the solution.

issues.description: Method setLectureName(...): In the solution (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java) the setter is declared as public void setLectureName(String lectureName) but the class field lectureName is of type LectureName. Assigning the String parameter to the LectureName field is a type mismatch and will not compile. The problem statement/UML models lectureName as a String, so the setter parameter should match that design.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the setter parameter type with the field type. To match the exercise UML, change the lectureName field and the constructor parameter to String so setLectureName(String) assigns directly to the String field. If LectureName was intended, change the setter signature to setLectureName(LectureName) and update any usages/tests to pass LectureName objects.
